title: Weight zero of the constant sheaf
statement:
On every separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, the constant
Weil sheaf $\Qlb$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight zero.

proof.text: Let $Y_0$ be the separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme in the statement, and take $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. The canonical constant $E$-Weil sheaf admits the normalized compatible integral constant datum by [lem-zl-constant-weil-datum]; its hypotheses are exactly separatedness, finite type and $\ell\neq p$. Apply the first assertion of [lem-zl-constant-sheaf-lseries] to this datum. For every closed point $y$, the one-circuit geometric local operator $F_y$ of that assertion, explicitly the operator of def-weil-local-frobenius-trace, is the identity on its degree-zero constant stalk $E$. This uses that lemma's geometric-operator assertion, not its Euler product or any global trace identity. In particular it is the full return operator at degree $[\kappa(y):k_0]$, including geometric-point transport, that is the identity.

proof.text: By clause 5 of [def-weil-constant-weil-structure], the canonical $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf is represented at the stage $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ by the very constant $E$-Weil sheaf used in Step 1. The common-stage stalk and local-operator convention of [def-weil-punctual-weights] takes $\mathrm H^0(C_E)\otimes_E\Qlb$ and the scalar extension of its local operator. Thus here the stalk is $E\otimes_E\Qlb\cong\Qlb$, by $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, and its local operator sends $a\otimes b$ to $F_y(a)\otimes b=a\otimes b$. Pure tensors span, so the common-stage local operator is the identity. This uses the common-stage construction itself and makes no identification with the distinct upstream ProEtaleWeilSheaf category.

proof.text: Fix any closed point $y$ and any local eigenvalue $\alpha\in\Qlb$. By the eigenvalue convention in [def-weil-punctual-weights], there is a nonzero stalk vector $v$ with $F_y(v)=\alpha v$. Step 2 gives $v=\alpha v$, hence $(\alpha-1)v=0$, and since $\Qlb$ is a field and $v\neq0$, $\alpha=1$. The field embedding $\iota$ sends $1$ to $1$, so $|\iota(\alpha)|=1=q_y^{0/2}$. This is the required purity condition at every closed point. If $Y_0$ is empty there are no such points, and the condition holds vacuously.
